page.text:
Abstract algebra investigates mathematical structures defined not by the
particular nature of their objects, but by the axiomatic identities
governing their internal operations. Rather than computing with numbers
of fixed ontological status, algebra abstracts the operations themselves,
isolating the minimal conditions required for deduction and calculation.

This chapter mounts an ascending staircase of algebraic structures
equipped with a single binary operation. Each step imposes precisely one
additional equational demand: beginning with an unconstrained closed
operation (a *magma*), we introduce associativity to obtain a
*semigroup*, adjoining a two-sided neutral element produces a *monoid*,
and guaranteeing two-sided inverses culminates in a *group*. This
incremental construction clarifies exactly which algebraic theorems
depend on associativity, which require an identity, and which necessitate
full invertibility.
